cues.text: An Announcement in Latin
On February 11, 2013, Pope Benedict XVI announced in Latin, before a small consistory of cardinals gathered for an unrelated matter, that he would resign the papacy effective February 28.
The declaration was so unexpected that several cardinals present did not immediately grasp its meaning.
It also made Benedict the first pope to resign the office in nearly six hundred years, since Gregory XII's resignation in 1415 had helped end the Western Schism.
Benedict's announcement came at the end of a pontificate lasting nearly eight years, following the long reign of John Paul II.
As Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, Benedict had served John Paul II for over two decades as Prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith before his own election in 2005.
A Body No Longer Equal to the Task
Benedict explained his decision plainly, citing his advanced age — he was eighty-five — and a declining strength of mind and body.
He judged them no longer adequate to the demands of the papal office in the modern world, a candor about the papacy's physical limits that had few real precedents in its long history.
He retired to a monastery within the Vatican gardens, adopting the title Pope Emeritus , and lived there in quiet prayer until his death in December 2022.
A Conclave in March
The College of Cardinals convened a conclave in Rome in early March 2013.
On March 13 , after just five ballots across two days, it elected Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio , Archbishop of Buenos Aires, Argentina.
He was the first pope from the Americas in the Church's entire history, and the first member of the Society of Jesus ever elected to the papacy.
A Name Never Before Chosen
Bergoglio took the name Francis , a name no previous pope had ever chosen, in deliberate honor of St. Francis of Assisi.
He honored the saint's example of poverty, simplicity, and care for creation—a choice he explained had come to him almost spontaneously during his election.
A fellow cardinal embraced him and whispered, "Don't forget the poor."
From his first appearance on the loggia of St. Peter's, Francis set a notably informal tone, asking the crowd to pray for him before offering his own blessing.
Legacy
The near-simultaneous resignation of one pope and election of another raised genuinely new questions about the Church's governance.
Without the intervening death that had marked every previous papal transition for six centuries, the papacy faced questions it had not addressed in the modern era.

Benedict's careful conduct as Pope Emeritus, largely withdrawn from public affairs and consistently deferential to his successor, did much to answer them through simple, deliberate example rather than any new formal precedent.
Francis went on to lead the Church for twelve years, until his own death in April 2025.
He was remembered for a pastoral style and priorities that marked a distinctive chapter in the modern papacy: mercy, the environment, migrants, and the peripheries of both Church and society.
